relation_to_present_study: Establishes transfer science; does not connect a harmonised global data chain
Provides matrix biotransfer screening; does not validate feed-origin attribution with global monitoring
Measures broad pesticide and veterinary-drug residues in Austrian dairy-cattle diets but not matched transfer into milk
Defines feed MRL framework for cattle and sheep; regulatory limits are not observed global exposure
Reviews analytical detection in animal-derived food; does not identify feed pathways
Demonstrates a local organochlorine feed-water-soil-to-milk pathway; not a multi-country trade attribution design
Prioritises European feed hazards; limited transfer data can yield unclassifiable hazards
Formalises food-safety knowledge-gap questions for circular systems; not a residue-specific admission chain
Connects corn production and processing to livestock dietary burden; does not add matched animal-food validation
Harmonises pesticide MRL relations in animal foods; MRLs remain regulatory values rather than occurrence
Ranks contaminants from fish feed to fillet; prioritisation is not a quantitative human exposure model
